reason: The text demonstrates Yahweh's care for the Hebrew people through multiple expressions: (1) God appoints David as shepherd ('you shall feed/shepherd my people Israel'), explicitly designating leadership to care for the people's welfare; (2) God provides military victories against the Philistines to protect Israel from external threats; (3) God blesses David's kingdom and reign; (4) David distributes material provisions (bread, meat, raisins) to all the people; (5) The overall narrative arc shows divine favor and providence guiding Israel toward unified stability under a chosen leader. The appointment of a shepherd-leader to feed and guide the people constitutes an expression of divine solicitude for their wellbeing.
